question: According to Census of India 2011, what was the population density of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**382 person/km2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the 2011 Census, India has a population density of 382 persons per square kilometer.
 
• The population density is calculated as the number of people living per unit area of land.
 
• India saw a growth in population density from 324 persons per sq km in 2001 to 382 persons per sq km in 2011.
 
• Higher population density indicates a higher concentration of people in a specific area, which can impact resources and infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Population Density

 
 
• Population density is a measurement of the number of people per unit area, usually per square kilometer or square mile.
 
• It is used to measure how crowded or sparsely populated an area is.
 
• High population density can lead to challenges such as congestion, pressure on resources, and environmental degradation.
 
• Conversely, low population density may indicate underutilization of resources and potentially lesser economic development.
 
 
 
• Census
 
 
• A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.
 
• In India, the census is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The data collected includes demographic, economic, and social information.
 
• The census provides vital statistics that aid in policy making and planning for the country's development.
 
 
 
• 2011 Census of India
 
 
• The 2011 Census of India was the 15th National Census since 1871.
 
• It was conducted in two phases: the house listing phase and the population enumeration phase.
 
• The data collected includes population size, density, sex ratio, literacy rate, and employment statistics.
 
• It provides a comprehensive picture of India's demographic and socio-economic status, which is crucial for governance and development planning.
